entries.subject: Transit times in TESS sectors 97, 105 and 106 (2025-2026)
entries.finding: Folded on the orbit's straight-line ephemeris (P 3.5852900 d, transit 2459169.27128 BJD; the TOI table's 396.02, uncertain by 8 min at these dates), the SPOC 2-minute light curves show no dip; with HR 858 c and d masked, the dip (229, 239 and 230 ppm; 29, 19 and 27 sigma) comes 294, 390 and 412 min early in sectors 97, 105 and 106, earlier by about 1.5 min per orbit. Bonfanti et al. (2024) report significant transit-timing variations of b and c, close to but out of the 5:3 resonance, with semi-amplitudes of up to 5 hours in their simulation. No archive product gives a TTV ephemeris, so the orbit stays the straight line and there is no transit chart.
entries.revisitWhen: A published TTV ephemeris or dynamical model of HR 858 b and c that preparation can call for the transit times.
